name: Sonos Era 300
summary: Sonos's spatial-audio speaker with an up-firing tweeter; great for Atmos music on its own and the best rear-surround upgrade for an Arc, Arc Ultra or Beam (Gen 2).
verdict:
The Era 300 is built for spatial audio: **six drivers** (four tweeters, including one firing straight up, plus two side-firing woofers), each with its own Class-D amplifier. Alone it plays Dolby Atmos music convincingly; in a home theater its real job is as a **rear surround with height**.

**System maths.** Pair two Era 300s as rears with a [Sonos Arc Ultra](/gear/sonos-arc-ultra/) and a [Sonos Sub 4](/gear/sonos-sub-4/) and you get a 7.1.4-style layout: the bar's front height channels plus the Era 300s' up-firing tweeters adding rear height. That's the closest a wireless system gets to a receiver-based [Dolby Atmos](/glossary/dolby-atmos/) setup with ceiling speakers, without running a single speaker cable (each Era 300 still needs an outlet).

**Placement.** Rear surrounds sound best roughly **110–135 degrees** from straight ahead, at or a little above ear height. The Era 300 must sit upright with its top clear, so use stands or the official wall mounts rather than tucking it on a bookshelf with a shelf above it, which blocks the up-firing tweeter.

**Compared with the [Era 100](/gear/sonos-era-100/)**, it costs roughly double but adds the height channel. For a Beam (Gen 2) or a 5.1 setup without overhead effects, the Era 100 pair is the better value. Trueplay tuning, Wi-Fi, AirPlay 2, Bluetooth and USB-C line-in round it out. See the [best wireless speakers for home theater](/best-wireless-speakers-for-home-theater/) roundup.

name: Bose Surround Speakers 700
summary: Compact wireless rear speakers for Bose smart soundbars that add genuine surround effects, but only work in the Bose ecosystem and cost a lot for their size.
verdict:
The Surround Speakers 700 are small, aluminum-finished rear speakers that connect by short cables to a **wireless receiver module**, which then links to a compatible Bose smart soundbar such as the [Bose Smart Ultra Soundbar](/gear/bose-smart-ultra-soundbar/) or [Bose Smart Soundbar](/gear/bose-smart-soundbar/). There's no streaming or standalone use; their only job is to put effects behind you.

**Why real rears beat virtual surround.** Even the best soundbar processing struggles to place sound convincingly behind the listener, because all the drivers sit in front. Two physical speakers at roughly **110–120 degrees** from center create true side and rear effects, which is the single biggest upgrade most bar owners can make after a subwoofer.

**Cost maths.** Add these and the [Bose Bass Module 700](/gear/bose-bass-module-700/) to a Smart Ultra and the total lands in the same range as the [Samsung HW-Q990F](/gear/samsung-hw-q990f/), which includes sub, rears and four height channels in the box. If you already own a Bose bar and like it, the 700s are the natural add-on; if you're starting from scratch, compare complete systems first.

**Placement and power.** The speakers are tiny and wall-mountable; the receiver module needs a power outlet near your seats. Owners praise the discreet size and seamless integration, while noting the price premium over the standard Bose Surround Speakers. See the [Bose home theater review](/bose-home-theater-review/).

name: Klipsch The Fives Powered Speakers
amazonQuery: Klipsch The Fives powered speakers HDMI ARC
summary: Powered Klipsch bookshelf speakers with HDMI ARC, a phono input and a sub output, making a simple, great-sounding stereo TV system without a receiver.
verdict:
The Fives are powered bookshelf speakers with a twist: an **HDMI ARC** input, so they connect straight to your TV and respond to its remote. Each speaker uses a **4.5-inch fiber-composite woofer** and a **1-inch titanium tweeter on a Tractrix horn**, giving the lively, dynamic Klipsch sound. Inputs also include optical, USB, a switchable phono/line input for a turntable, Bluetooth and a **subwoofer output**.

**Stereo isn't surround, so set the TV correctly.** Over ARC the Fives receive stereo PCM. Set your TV's audio output to PCM or stereo so it downmixes 5.1 soundtracks; dialogue then comes from a phantom center between the speakers.

**Placement maths.** For a good stereo image, form an equilateral triangle: if your sofa is **8 feet** from the TV wall, aim for the speakers about **6–8 feet** apart, angled slightly toward you. Put them at ear height or tilt them up, since the horn tweeters are directional.

**Add a sub.** The 4.5-inch woofers are fine for TV and music but don't reach deep movie bass. Use the sub out with a compact sub such as the [Klipsch R-120SW](/gear/klipsch-r-120sw/) or [SVS SB-1000 Pro](/gear/svs-sb-1000-pro/) for a capable 2.1 system.

Compared with a soundbar, you get far better stereo separation and music playback, but no virtual surround or Atmos. See the [best wireless speakers for home theater](/best-wireless-speakers-for-home-theater/) and [soundbar vs home theater](/soundbar-vs-home-theater/).

name: KEF LS50 Wireless II
summary: KEF's acclaimed all-in-one active speakers with Uni-Q drivers, 380 W per speaker, HDMI eARC and every major streaming service; audiophile stereo for a TV setup.
verdict:
The LS50 Wireless II packs a complete hi-fi into two speakers. Each has KEF's **5.25-inch Uni-Q driver** (a 0.75-inch aluminum tweeter mounted in the center of the woofer) with **Metamaterial Absorption Technology**, driven by **380 W per speaker**: 100 W for the tweeter and 280 W for the woofer. KEF rates frequency response at **45 Hz–28 kHz ±3 dB**.

**Why that matters on a TV.** The HDMI [eARC](/glossary/earc/) input means the TV and its remote control the speakers directly, and the coaxial Uni-Q design gives an unusually wide, consistent sweet spot, so people off to the side of the sofa still hear a stable center image for dialogue.

**Add a sub at the right crossover.** 45 Hz at ±3 dB is excellent for a 5.25-inch woofer, but movie [LFE](/glossary/lfe/) goes well below that. Use the sub output and the app's high-pass filter: crossing the speakers over at around **80 Hz** frees the woofers from the deepest bass, which lowers distortion and raises clean output. A sealed sub like the [SVS SB-2000 Pro](/gear/svs-sb-2000-pro/) blends well.

**Connections.** Optical, coaxial, analog, Ethernet, Bluetooth, AirPlay 2, Chromecast, Spotify Connect, Tidal Connect and Roon Ready. It's stereo only; there's no surround decoding.

Independent measurements show excellent performance, and owners rate it among the best active speakers available. It's expensive, but it replaces a streamer, amplifier and speakers. See the [best wireless speakers for home theater](/best-wireless-speakers-for-home-theater/).

name: Sonos Era 100
summary: A compact Sonos speaker with true stereo from one box, Bluetooth and line-in, and the most cost-effective way to add rear surrounds to a Sonos soundbar.
verdict:
The Era 100 is Sonos's compact speaker: **two angled tweeters** and a **woofer**, each with its own Class-D amplifier, so a single unit plays in stereo. It adds Bluetooth and a USB-C line-in (with adapter), plus Trueplay tuning.

**As rear surrounds.** A pair of Era 100s is the most cost-effective way to turn a [Sonos Beam (Gen 2)](/gear/sonos-beam-gen-2/) or [Sonos Arc Ultra](/gear/sonos-arc-ultra/) into a real surround system. Add a [Sonos Sub 4](/gear/sonos-sub-4/) and you have a wireless 5.1 with the bar doing front height duty on the Arc Ultra. Compared with [Era 300](/gear/sonos-era-300/) rears, you give up rear height effects but pay about half.

**Placement maths.** Put surrounds about **110–120 degrees** from straight ahead, slightly above ear height. On a typical sofa that means beside or just behind the seats. If the speakers must sit on a back wall, angle them toward the listening position and let Trueplay balance levels.

**Stereo pair for music or TV.** Two Era 100s also make a capable stereo pair. In a room where you sit 8 feet away, aim for them roughly 6–8 feet apart.

The size limits deep bass, and each speaker needs an outlet. Owners rate the clarity and value highly. See the [best wireless speakers for home theater](/best-wireless-speakers-for-home-theater/) and [Sonos home theater review](/sonos-home-theater-review/).

name: Edifier S3000Pro Wireless Speakers
summary: Active stereo speakers with planar tweeters, a wireless link between left and right, and balanced XLR inputs; strong music performance with a simple TV connection over optical.
verdict:
The S3000Pro is Edifier's flagship active stereo pair. Each speaker combines an **aluminum-cone woofer** with a **planar diaphragm tweeter**, and the two speakers link **wirelessly** to each other, so no cable has to cross the TV wall between them (each speaker still needs power). Inputs include **balanced XLR**, RCA, optical, coaxial and Bluetooth with **aptX HD**.

**Connecting to a TV: set PCM.** There's no HDMI, so the usual route is optical from the TV. Most active speakers like this don't decode Dolby or DTS bitstreams, so set your TV's digital audio output to **PCM**; otherwise you may get silence or noise from streaming apps that send Dolby Digital. The TV then downmixes 5.1 to stereo.

**Placement maths.** Wireless between speakers means freedom on spacing: for a sofa about 9 feet away, place them roughly 7–9 feet apart, slightly toed in, tweeters at ear height.

**Who it suits.** Owners and reviewers praise the detailed, extended treble from the planar tweeters and strong overall value for music. For a TV, you give up HDMI convenience and remote integration compared with the [Klipsch The Fives](/gear/klipsch-the-fives/) or [KEF LS50 Wireless II](/gear/kef-ls50-wireless-ii/).

See the [best wireless speakers for home theater](/best-wireless-speakers-for-home-theater/) roundup.
